professor.name: Dr. Okafor
professor.post: Many universities now offer the same courses both online and in person. Some people believe online courses are just as effective as traditional classes, while others think students learn better when they are physically present. Which format do you think is better for learning, and why?

students.name: Lena
students.post: I prefer online courses. I can watch the lectures again when I don't understand something, and I can study at the times when I am most focused. It also saves me two hours of travel every day.

students.name: Marcus
students.post: For me, in-person classes are much better. When I'm in a classroom, I can ask questions immediately and discuss ideas with classmates. At home I get distracted easily and it's hard to stay motivated.

professor.name: Dr. Chen
professor.post: Some cities have made public transportation free for all residents, paying for it with taxes. Supporters say it reduces traffic and pollution; critics say the money could be used better elsewhere. Should cities make public transportation free? Explain your view.

students.name: Sofia
students.post: Yes. If buses and trains were free, many more people would leave their cars at home. That would mean less traffic, cleaner air and fewer accidents, which also saves the city money.

students.name: Daniel
students.post: I'm not convinced. Making transport free does not fix the real problem, which is that buses are often slow and unreliable. The city should invest in better service first, not in free tickets.
